purpose: Apply accepted chain grouping, proposition-polarity corrections, chain-level findings, and plain-English inferential explanations after the sealed historical evidence-adjudication input has been validated.

CH-F15E-CSAR-URANIUM.public_title: F-15E shootdown, missing airman, rescue, and uranium narrative
CH-F15E-CSAR-URANIUM.plain_english_summary: A real F-15E was lost and one airman was genuinely missing. The deceptive narrative was what Iranian official and state-media channels said happened next: the aircraft was first misidentified as an F-35; a capture story was promoted while Iranian authorities were still searching for the airman; rescue failure and Iranian-caused equipment losses were overstated; false remains evidence was presented; and, after both crew were recovered, the story shifted toward a nuclear/uranium mission explanation. Atlas keeps the real shootdown, the missing-airman period, the later F-15E correction, and real rescue-equipment losses as factual context rather than labeling those facts themselves as lies.
how_we_know: The underlying loss is real: a U.S. F-15E went down in Iran and one crew member remained missing while U.S. forces searched for him.
The original F-35 identification was wrong. Iranian reporting later corrected the aircraft type to F-15E using recovered wreckage and debris.

The capture branch is false, not merely unsupported. Tasnim reported that the missing airman was likely captured; a provincial IRGC unit later denied he had been captured or detained, Iranian authorities were still seeking his capture, and the airman was subsequently recovered by U.S. forces.
The early fact that the second airman had not yet been recovered was true. The categorical claim that the rescue ultimately failed was not: both crew members were recovered.

U.S. rescue aircraft and equipment were genuinely lost or damaged, but that does not establish Iran destroyed all of it. Independent reconstruction attributes part of the destroyed rescue package to U.S. denial action after aircraft became disabled.
Iranian official channels also presented supposed U.S. remains as evidence; the Iranian broadcasting system acknowledged the image was inaccurate or incorrect the next day.

Iran really did possess enriched uranium at Isfahan. That fact is not evidence that the observed rescue package was secretly a uranium-seizure mission. After the personnel-recovery outcome was established, later reporting substituted a nuclear/uranium mission narrative while preserving the same claimed Iranian victory.

The Lie finding comes from the combined chronology: repeated contradictions, corrections available inside the same state information system, direct institutional access to wreckage and battle-damage information, and later outcome-preserving narrative substitution. It is not based merely on the absence of proof or on a U.S. denial.

CH-AIRCRAFT-KILL-AGGREGATES.public_title: Iranian U.S. aircraft and UAV cumulative kill-count narrative
CH-AIRCRAFT-KILL-AGGREGATES.plain_english_summary: Iran has reported a changing series of aircraft/UAV totals, but the denominator and metric do not stay constant: mixed drones, aircraft hit, aircraft targeted, and later type-specific MQ-9 ordinals are different propositions. Atlas therefore keeps each count and metric branch separate instead of treating the series as one cumulative confirmed-kill ledger.
how_we_know: The public series moves through 82, more than 130, 170, more than 170 aircraft hit including 16 fighters, and a 210 figure whose headline/body use different verbs.
Those figures are not interchangeable: drones downed, aircraft hit, aircraft targeted, and type-specific MQ-9 losses use different denominators and effects.

The Apr. 28 '16 fighters hit' proposition is distinct from the analytic question of whether that metric can be compared directly with earlier drone-down totals; the old model accidentally duplicated the same proposition ID for both.

The May 26 article itself provides the contradiction: the headline says about 210 were downed while the body reports language about being able to target around 210. The publication act is observable; the underlying '210 downed' assertion is the factual proposition.

Later 52nd/53rd MQ-9 ordinals require a type-specific reconciled ledger. Existing evidence supports substantial real MQ-9 attrition but does not establish those exact ordinals as either true or false.

CH-TURKEY-MISSILE-DENIAL.public_title: Turkey missile incident: denial, attribution, and false-flag substitution
CH-TURKEY-MISSILE-DENIAL.plain_english_summary: Iran repeatedly denied that the missiles came from Iran. After Turkish/NATO attribution accumulated, the public explanation changed to a false-flag theory. Atlas treats the earlier launch denials, the later causal theory, and the observable narrative substitution as separate propositions.
how_we_know: The first three categorical no-Iran-launch statements conflict with later Turkish/NATO attribution.
The later false-flag causal mechanism remains unsubstantiated on the current record.
What is independently observable is the chronology: the false-flag explanation appeared after the earlier categorical denials and after contrary attribution accumulated.

CH-QATAR-PILOTS.public_title: Missing Iranian pilots and Qatar custody-access narrative

public_finding.label: False custody claim; likely lie on obstruction branch

CH-QATAR-PILOTS.plain_english_summary: Iranian aircraft and aircrew really were lost or went missing in the Qatar fighting. That factual baseline was incorrectly marked false in the old Ledger. The later claim that three missing pilots were alive in secret Qatari custody is a separate false proposition, and the subsequent claim that Qatar had simply kept an Iranian fact-finding team waiting for months is independently adjudicated as a likely lie.
how_we_know: The underlying Iranian aircraft/aircrew losses and missing-person problem are independently established; they are factual context, not the disputed custody claim.
Qatar denied secretly holding the pilots, reported recovery of one pilot's remains, and described an April invitation for Iran to review the search-and-rescue record.
The secret-custody allegation is therefore false on the completed record, while claimant knowledge remains less certain because Iran did not control Qatari detention systems.

The later obstruction claim is different. Qatar says it formally invited an Iranian team in April, Iran did not respond, and senior Iranian-Qatari diplomatic contact was already occurring. That makes the broad 'kept waiting for months' story materially harder to explain as simple lack of access.

Atlas does not let the false custody allegation contaminate the real aircraft-loss baseline, and does not let the stronger knowledge finding on the obstruction branch propagate backward to every earlier statement.

CH-INDIAN-OCEAN-DESTROYER.public_title: Indian Ocean U.S. destroyer/supply-ship strike narrative

CH-ALUDEID-BDA.plain_english_summary: Al Udeid suffered real, serious damage. The forensic question is the level of effect: radar/site damage and CAOC inoperability are supported, permanent destruction of the radar remains unresolved, and shorthand that the entire base was destroyed or unusable overstates the evidence. The old Ledger also carried a second shorthand Al Udeid chain for the same physical event; that duplicate is folded into this event chain as context.
how_we_know: Independent satellite imagery and later reporting confirm material strike damage at Al Udeid.
The AN/FPS-132 site was physically hit and materially degraded; available public evidence does not settle permanent repairability.
Separate reporting supports that the Combined Air Operations Center was rendered inoperable.
Those subfacility effects do not establish that the entire air base ceased operating.
The separate social-media shorthand record concerns the same physical event and therefore belongs inside this chain, not as another top-level event card.

CH-KUWAIT-F15-FRIENDLY-FIRE.public_title: Kuwait F-15 losses: Iranian attribution versus friendly-fire finding

CH-BUSHEHR-AIRCRAFT.plain_english_summary: Iranian reporting said a U.S. aircraft had been destroyed near Bushehr/Jam. The physical-loss proposition is contradicted by the available record and should be counted as the accusation it is, rather than hidden as non-accusation context. Current evidence does not establish claimant knowledge strongly enough for a Lie finding.
how_we_know: CENTCOM said all U.S. aircraft were accounted for.
No independently verified wreckage, serial, or corresponding U.S. aircraft loss was identified in the reviewed record.
That is sufficient for the current FALSE finding, but the present evidence package does not establish what the original local/state-media source knew when it reported the claim.
